title: OpenAI Merges ChatGPT Chat and Work into One Usage Meter
summary: OpenAI rolls unified ChatGPT usage meter for Pro subscribers, combining Chat and Work buckets. Instant model stays unlimited. Broader rollout in December 2026.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- OpenAI began merging ChatGPT Chat and Work into one shared usage meter for a small group of Pro subscribers on November 25, 2026.
- Most users will see no change, but the heaviest users may hit limits sooner under the combined allowance.
- Instant model conversations remain unlimited and do not count toward the new shared meter, with broader rollout planned for December 2026.


OpenAI started routing both ChatGPT Chat and Work traffic through a single shared usage meter for a small group of Pro subscribers on November 25, 2026, marking a significant shift in how the company allocates compute resources. The change, announced by product lead Thibault Sottiaux on X, combines what were previously separate usage buckets into one unified allowance. While most subscribers will not see more frequent resets, OpenAI acknowledged that a small fraction of its heaviest users may hit limits sooner under the new system.


## How the Unified Meter Works


Under the new structure, conversations in both Chat and Work modes now draw from the same shared allowance for ChatGPT Pro subscribers. OpenAI emphasized that conversations using the Instant model remain unlimited and do not count toward the combined meter, giving users an unrestricted fallback option when they exhaust their monthly allocation. Subscribers who hit their limit can continue using Instant without interruption, though they lose access to more advanced reasoning models until their meter resets.


## Release Date and Rollout Timeline


Officially launched on November 25, 2026, the unified meter is currently available to a limited test group of Pro subscribers. OpenAI plans to expand the rollout more broadly in December 2026, bringing the consolidated usage system to the full Pro subscriber base. The phased approach allows the company to monitor impact and adjust allocation policies before wider deployment.


## User Reaction and Compute Pressure


Pro subscribers pushed back on social media and OpenAI's community forum throughout the day, expressing concern that the combined bucket effectively reduces their access to advanced reasoning models while subscription fees remain unchanged. An OpenAI representative told TechCrunch the company will "continue working to improve efficiency so subscribers could get more out of their plans." The move mirrors a similar consolidation Anthropic ran in September 2026, when it folded Claude chat and Cowork into a single interface. Compute-cost pressure has been a recurring theme across more than 430 OpenAI stories logged in the past 90 days.


## What This Means


The unified meter represents OpenAI's latest effort to balance user demand with infrastructure costs as advanced reasoning models consume more compute per request. For most ChatGPT Pro subscribers, day-to-day usage will remain unchanged, but power users who previously relied on separate Chat and Work allowances may need to adjust their workflows or rely more heavily on the unlimited Instant tier. As OpenAI refines efficiency and scales its infrastructure, the company will likely continue iterating on allocation policies to keep Pro subscriptions economically sustainable while delivering value to subscribers.
